en: The Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas, Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
2. The Second Story of the Throne-Vimāna “Your sublime throne is made of beryl;
swift as thought, it goes wherever you desire.”
Adorned with garlands, wearing fine clothes,
you shine like lightning upon a mountain peak.
By what means do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those riches that are dear to the mind arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she explained the deed whose fruit this is:
"When I was among humans, having become a human being..."
I gave a seat to those who had arrived;
I paid homage and joined my palms in salutation,
and I gave gifts according to my means.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this;
because of that, I prosper here;
and wealth arises for me.
"Whatever is dear to the mind—
O monk of great power, I shall tell you— those who,
having become human, performed meritorious deeds."
Thus was my power so blazing that my complexion shone forth in all directions.
Thus ends the second *Pīṭhavimāna*.
